To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a common variant in the FADS gene cluster is associated with the production of leukotriene and 5-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid (5-HETE) in human whole blood.
a common variant in the FADS gene cluster is associated with the synthesis of 12/15-LOX products, leukotrienes, and thromboxanes in humans.

the genetic variants in the Fatty acid desaturase cluster (rs174537) are associated with leukotrine B4 and 20-HETE generation from stimulated human blood and that these genetic variants are associated with the capacity of the liver to synthesize long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids (ARA/LA) and 20-HDPE.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of genetic variation in the regulation of eicosanoid synthesis.
the role of fatty acids in the development of chronic disease.
the role of dietary fatty acids in the pathogenesis of chronic inflammatory disease, and the genetic factors that determine the capacity to synthesize inflammatory mediators from dietary precursors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the FADS variant rs174537 is not only associated with the synthesis of arachidonic acids but is also associated with the synthesis and release of leukotriene and 5-Hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acids from stimulated whole blood.
this is an interesting paper which adds to our understanding of how genetic variants in the FADs cluster affect eicosanoid metabolism.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a genetic variant in the FADS gene cluster affects the synthesis of eicosanoids from stimulated human blood, specifically 5-lipoxygene products.

genetic variation in FADS influences the production of leukotriene and 5-HetE, but not prostaglandins.
